A layer of a map

Source: R/map.R
rr_layer.Rd

One layer of an rr_map(): what it shows, how it is drawn, and where its data come from. Five kinds:

Usage

rr_layer(
  id,
  kind = c("grid", "vector", "geojson", "dem", "contour"),
  label = id,
  info = NULL,
  visible = TRUE,
  tiles = NULL,
  meta = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  style = NULL,
  popup = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  variants = NULL,
  count = NULL,
  missing = NULL,
  filters = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  source_layer = NULL,
  minzoom = NULL,
  maxzoom = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  encoding = NULL,
  tile_size = NULL,
  bounds = NULL,
  shade = NULL,
  colour = NULL,
  contours = NULL,
  state = NULL
)

Arguments

id

The layer's name, lower case: its checkbox, its source and its key in the page's address.

kind

"grid", "vector", "geojson", "dem" or "contour".

label, info

Its name in the sidebar and the text behind its ⓘ.

visible

Whether it is on when the page opens; the address turns it off with id=0 or on with id=1.

tiles

The tile function. For a grid, function(z, x, y, params), params a named list of the filters' values as text (absent when not given); for a vector layer, function(z, x, y). It returns a Mapbox vector tile as raw bytes (DuckDB's ST_AsMVT()), or raw(0). A dem layer's, function(z, x, y), returns an image of elevations (PNG or WebP) as raw bytes, or NULL where there is none; a contour layer's the same.

meta

For a grid, a list or a function returning one, read when the server starts: options (per filter with meta = TRUE, a data frame of value and, optionally, name and code), ranges (per range filter, its first and last value) and v (a version, put into the tile address so a rebuilt source is not hidden by the browser's cache).

data

For a geojson layer: GeoJSON text, an sf object, or a function returning either, read when the server starts.

style

A list of MapLibre layer specifications, without source (the layer's own).

popup

For a vector or geojson layer, what a click shows: click (the style ids that answer), title (a field), fields (each a list of field, label, and optionally values, a value-to-text lookup whose text may hold {field} placeholders; template, a text with {field} placeholders shown in place of the value when there is one; and format, "value" or "count"), maxWidth. For a grid, fields only, the first in bold. Opt-in, a label on hover: hover, the style ids whose features show their title in a light label beside the pointer while it is over them (TRUE for those of click), and hover_fields, TRUE to show the fields there too. Over features of several layers, the topmost speaks, as for a click; a click hides the label until the pointer is over another feature. Opt-in, a verdict on each feature, kept by a server started with rr_serve(verdicts = ): verdict, a list of field (the field naming a feature: a verdict belongs to its value), questions (one to four, each an id, a label, two to six options and optionally skip), and text (TRUE for a note on the feature, in the reader's words). An option is a value (letters, digits, _ or -), a label (a text or a key of the map's texts), optionally a colour for the feature's mark (the first green by default, the others red), and other = TRUE for an answer that names another feature: a box for its name, the names in view offered. skip names earlier questions and the answers that leave this one out (list(name = "not")). One question may be given as options alone. store, another layer's id, keeps the answers under that layer's and shows its answers (two layers of one kind of feature: a feature's answer the same whichever it is clicked on); the two must ask the same questions. The click's popup then holds the questions, a button for each answer; each answer is written to the server's file with the feature's place, and a mark drawn on the feature (the first question's colour its fill, the second's its ring). A later answer replaces the earlier; rr_verdicts() reads them.

legend

A list of swatches, each swatch (fill and stroke, or dot) and label.

variants

For a vector, geojson or dem layer, styles to choose between in the page, such as the column the points are coloured by: label (the control's text) and options, each a value, a label, paint (by the layer's style ids, the paint properties it sets) and optionally legend (in place of the layer's). The first option is shown when the page opens; a choice goes into the address as <id>_by, and nothing is fetched again.

count

The text beside its label: text (a key whose {1} is the count) and, for geojson, where (a field and the value of the features to count). A vector layer's count is its tile function's count attribute.

missing

The text shown when the server has none of it.

filters

For a grid: a list of controls, each a list with id, label and one of: options (a list of value, label and optionally tip) with an optional default; meta = TRUE (options from meta, with an optional unnamed text for an option with no name; several values, comma separated, may come from the address); type = "range" with params (two names, such as c("y1", "y2"), its bounds from meta); type = "metric" (the choice among metrics).

metrics

For a grid: a list of the numeric fields it can be coloured by, each field and label.

source_layer

For a grid, the tile layer its cells are in ("cells").

minzoom, maxzoom

The zooms its tiles are made for.

opacity

For a grid, its opacity when the page opens, 0-100.

encoding, tile_size, bounds

For a dem or contour layer: how its images hold the elevation ("terrarium" or "mapbox"), their side in pixels, and the extent that has tiles (west, south, east, north), so the page asks for no other. Taken, with minzoom and maxzoom, from the attributes of tiles where not given (rr_tiles_mbtiles() sets them); else "terrarium" and 512. The image format ("png" or "webp") is the format attribute's.

shade

For a dem layer with a hillshade style: the relief's controls in the page, and their values when it opens, a list of any of method ("standard", "basic", "combined", "igor" or "multidirectional", three lights 45 degrees apart), direction (the light's azimuth, 0-359), altitude (0-90), exaggeration (the intensity, 0-1), opacity (0-100: the alpha of the shading's colours, which has no opacity of its own), shadow and highlight (colours as "#rrggbb"); MapLibre's own defaults for those not given, but an intensity of 0.6 and a dark blue-grey shadow, "#1b2a3a", as a bathymetry map in use settled on. TRUE takes every default. Each control applies as it moves, and goes into the page's address as <id>_method, <id>_dir, <id>_alt, <id>_ex, <id>_op, <id>_shadow and <id>_light. With fit, TRUE or a function of the view's box as a colour's fit returning a list with exaggeration (0-1), the intensity can follow the view (auto, TRUE by default; <id>_auto in the address, which leaves out <id>_ex while it follows), until it is set by hand. Tiles from rr_tiles_dem() are fitted in the page when no fit is given.

colour

For a dem layer with a color-relief style: its values in colour, with their controls in the page, a list of any of of ("depth", the elevation's negative, or "elevation"; what is 0 or less is clear), palettes (the ids of the palettes its control offers, of the map's palettes) and palette (the one it opens on), floor and cap (the values the palette's ends stand at, 1-10,000, set on one slider of two handles), scale ("log", "linear" or, with a fit, "equal"), mode ("ramp" or "bands"), bands (the bands' breaks, rising), cuts (the cuts offered, 0 for none) and cut (one of them: values under it are drawn as cut_as, "clear" or "grey"), opacity (0-100). Defaults: depth; for a depth the seven looks of rr_palettes() (quiet, seabed, deep, chart, grey, drained and haxby), for an elevation every palette of the map; the first of them; floor 10, cap 2,000; in equal shares with a fit, else log; a ramp; bands at 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1,000 and 2,000; cuts 0, 10, 20 and 50, no cut, clear; 100. TRUE takes them all. Another palette, such as "magma", is offered by naming it, colour = list(palettes = c("quiet", "magma")) (a palette not among palettes is put first in them), and one of your own by adding it to the map's, rr_map(palettes = c(rr_palettes(), list(list(id = "mine", label = "mine", colors = <colours>)))). Each control applies as it moves, and goes into the page's address as <id>_pal, <id>_lo, <id>_hi, <id>_scale, <id>_mode, <id>_cut, <id>_cutas and <id>_cop. With fit, the page has a "Fit to view" button and follows the view: it fits again each time the map settles, until a floor or cap is set by hand (auto, TRUE by default; <id>_auto in the address, where the floor and cap are left out while it follows). fit = TRUE makes the fit in the page from the layer's tiles in view, with no call to R (by the rules of rr_bundle()'s fit): the floor and the cap and the values' quantiles, which also offer scale "equal", each colour an equal share of the values in view between the floor and the cap. Or fit is a function of the view's west, south, east and north, answered by the server at /fit/<id>?bbox=w,s,e,n, returning the floor and the cap for the values there (or NULL where there are none; or a list of floor, cap and quantiles, the values' quantiles rising); a bundle fits in the page all the same. Tiles from rr_tiles_dem() are fitted in the page when no fit is given.

contours

For a contour layer: thresholds, a named list by zoom of the minor and the major interval from that zoom on (list("6" = c(500, 1000), "9" = c(50, 200)); a major line has level 1), and multiplier, by which the elevations are multiplied before the lines are drawn (-1 for depths, 1 by default). With fit, TRUE or a function as a colour's fit returning a list with the quantiles of the values in view, the lines can follow the view (auto, TRUE by default; <id>_auto in the address): about a dozen levels at round values near the view's quantiles, so the lines fall where the area is, drawn at a step of 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten that makes some 40 of the view's range; unticked, the thresholds and the style's filters. Tiles from rr_tiles_dem() are fitted in the page when no fit is given (by depth with a negative multiplier, else by elevation).

state

For a vector, geojson, dem or contour layer: values in the reader's hands that its style reads, in a filter, a paint or a layout property, as list("global-state", "<id>_<name>") (MapLibre's global state), such as whether a style is drawn, its colour, or a shift of the zoom it starts at. A list of controls, each with id (<name> above: lower-case letters and digits) and label, and either options (a list of value, a single number, text or TRUE/FALSE, and label), a list to choose from, with default one of the values (the first when not given); or no options and default TRUE or FALSE, a checkbox. Each applies as it changes, nothing fetched again, and goes into the page's address as <id>_<name>. Every one must be read by the style.

Value

An rr_layer, for rr_section().

Details

  • "grid": vector tiles of cells, coloured in the page by a numeric field on a log scale, with the palette, stretch, floor, cap and histogram there too. Its filters become controls whose values go into the tile address (one grid per map).

  • "vector": vector tiles of features, drawn by style, such as a table of geometries served by rr_tiles_table().

  • "geojson": features sent whole as GeoJSON, drawn by style.

  • "dem": image tiles of elevations (Terrarium or Mapbox Terrain-RGB), such as an MBTiles file read by rr_tiles_mbtiles(), drawn by style in the page under the base map's labels: MapLibre's hillshade and color-relief layers, so the shading and the colours are made in the browser.

  • "contour": contour lines made in the browser from the same image tiles of elevations, by maplibre-contour (loaded by the page only for a map that has one), at the intervals of contours, drawn by style (a line, and a symbol for the labels, from the source layer "contours", its features' ele and level) under the base map's labels.

Texts (label, info, a filter's label, a legend's label, ...) are keys of the map's texts (rr_map()), or the text itself where no key matches. MapLibre styles and expressions are lists, so that a one-element array stays an array in JSON: list("get", "kind"), list("zoom"); read from JSON with jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE) they already are.

See also

rr_map(), rr_tiles_table()

Examples

# A vector layer: the harbours as areas, a click shows the harbour's id
# \donttest{
harbours <- rr_layer(
  "harbours", "vector", label = "Harbours",
  tiles = rr_tiles_table(rr_example("dansk_harbours"), properties = "SI_HARB"),
  style = list(list(id = "harbours-fill", type = "fill", "source-layer" = "features",
                    paint = list("fill-color" = "#d9822b"))),
  popup = list(click = "harbours-fill", title = "SI_HARB")
)
# }

# A grid: its tile function is given the filters' values in `params`. This one returns an
# empty tile; a real one returns DuckDB's ST_AsMVT() of the cells (see the "Maps in RStudio"
# article).
cells <- rr_layer(
  "cells", "grid", label = "Pings by cell",
  tiles = function(z, x, y, params) raw(0),
  filters = list(
    list(id = "behaviour", label = "Behaviour",
         options = list(list(value = "", label = "all"),
                        list(value = "Fishing", label = "fishing"))),
    list(id = "metric", type = "metric", label = "Metric")
  ),
  metrics = list(list(field = "n", label = "pings"))
)

# A geojson layer: features sent whole, here one point
point <- rr_layer(
  "point", "geojson", label = "A point",
  data = '{"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [{"type": "Feature", "properties": {},
           "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [12.6, 56.0]}}]}',
  style = list(list(id = "point-dot", type = "circle", paint = list("circle-color" = "#c0392b")))
)
names(cells$config)
#> [1] "id"      "kind"    "label"   "visible" "filters" "metrics"
